summary:
AGROX is an interactive Agricultural Digital Twin and decision-support platform that transforms NASA Earth observation data into actionable field-level management and crop rotation strategies. Starting from an interactive 3D globe powered by NASA GIBS, farmers and agronomists can draw or locate any parcel worldwide—or explore our 144-hectare Story County, Iowa reference farm—to analyze zone-by-zone conditions and step into a 3D topographic farm twin.

We address the challenge of bridging raw satellite telemetry and everyday farming decisions by fusing NASA POWER daily agroclimatology (40+ years of temperature, precipitation, solar radiation, and drought indices), MODIS and Sentinel-2 NDVI time series, NASA SMAP soil moisture, and NASADEM terrain with FAO-56 daily root-zone water balance, growing degree days (GDD), and EcoCrop agroclimatic models. Every metric is transparently badged by data provenance (MEASURED, SIMULATED, ESTIMATED, or DECLARED).

As climate volatility, water scarcity, and soil degradation threaten global food security, AGROX empowers producers to simulate drought and irrigation scenarios and choose resilient multi-year crop rotations before planting.
details:
agroX is a web application that helps farmers and agricultural advisors explore what to plant, and in what order, as climate conditions change. Built for the NASA Space Apps Field Shift challenge, it combines NASA POWER weather data, satellite imagery, soil information, and crop characteristics in one interactive tool.

Users select or draw a field on a globe, explore its conditions in a 3D digital twin, and compare crop rotations based on local conditions and their priorities. A What If tool lets them adjust rainfall or temperature and see how the simulated crop response and rotation rankings change. In our Iowa pilot, a scenario with 20% less rainfall increased simulated water stress for corn from 11 to 25 days in one zone.

agroX makes Earth observation data easier to use in farm planning. By showing what drives each comparison, it helps farmers and advisors discuss options before planting.
